title: Structure and Dynamics of Bose Polarons across the Mott-Insulator to Superfluid Transition
authors: Ragheed Alhyder, Alessio Recati, Georg M. Bruun
abstract: A mobile impurity particle immersed in a quantum degenerate gas leads to the formation of a quasiparticle, which can   serve as a sensor for its environment. Here, we develop a unified wave function description of an impurity in a two-dimensional Bose-Hubbard model across the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition. Using a multi-mode variational ansatz based on the quantum Gutzwiller approach, we show that   the impurity can form several kinds of polaronic and molecular states. In addition to their spectral properties, the   wave function provides direct access to the microscopic structure of these states, and we demonstrate that strong correlations in the critical regime of the quantum phase transition give rise to several non-analytic features in the polaron properties. Increasing the impurity-boson interaction leads to transitions between polaron and molecular ground states, and the number of bosons in the impurity dressing cloud grows rapidly at the quantum critical point as the bath modes soften. We furthermore reveal qualitatively distinct non-equilibrium many-body dynamics after the injection of the impurity in the different phases of the Bose-Hubbard model. Our spectral, real space, and dynamical predictions describe complementary properties of   polarons in a strongly correlated bosonic bath, which can be observed using current techniques with atoms in optical lattices.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how an impurity particle forms a quasiparticle, or polaron, when immersed in a Bose gas undergoing a Mott-Insulator to Superfluid transition. Using a variational approach, the authors map out the polaron's structure and dynamics, showing that strong correlations near the critical point lead to unique, measurable features in its spectral properties and time evolution.
main_problem: The study focuses on developing a unified description of a mobile impurity particle (polaron) immersed in a quantum degenerate Bose gas as it undergoes a phase transition from a Mott Insulator (MI) to a Superfluid (SF) state.
main_result: The impurity forms various polaron and molecular states, exhibiting non-analytic features near the quantum critical point, and the system's dynamics are strongly dictated by the surrounding bosonic phase.
method: The authors employ a multi-mode variational ansatz based on the quantum Gutzwiller approach, solving a generalized eigenvalue problem derived from the Bose-Hubbard model Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system models an impurity interacting with a bath of bosons described by the 2D Bose-Hubbard model, characterized by hopping (J), on-site repulsion (U), and impurity-boson interaction ($U_{IB}$).
key_observables: Impurity spectral function, real space impurity-boson density correlation function $G(r)$, and non-equilibrium Ramsey contrast $|A(t)|$.
important_parameters: The ratio of interaction strengths ($U_{IB}/U$) and the ratio of hopping to repulsion ($J/U$), particularly near the quantum critical point (QCP).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a variational ansatz truncated to include up to two excitations of the bosons, and the time evolution is calculated using time-stepped Arnoldi/Lanczos methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the impurity spectral function across different interaction regimes, and plots show the dependence of wave function components and density correlations on the interaction strength, highlighting changes at the QCP.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the ground state structure (spectral properties, density correlations) and the non-equilibrium dynamics (Ramsey contrast) of the polaron across the MI-SF transition, detailing how the underlying bosonic phase dictates the quasiparticle behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed, quantitative predictions for how local impurities interact with strongly correlated quantum fluids, offering a theoretical framework applicable to ultracold atomic experiments in optical lattices.
